text: Your team says never log personal data. This repository says log full requests while debugging. When two rules disagree, which one does the AI follow?
Rule one: the stronger rule wins. Mandatory beats required, beats recommended, beats advisory. And a mandatory rule is never overridden, however close the other one is.
Rule two: between rules of the same strength, the closer one wins. Built-in, then you, your dōjō, a workspace, and finally the repository.
Sensei gathers every rule that applies, sorts by strength then scope, locks the mandatory ones, and merges duplicates. The same order, every time.
You can start from packs that already work: security, test-first, clean code, SOLID, compliance, UX, a minimal-solution pack, and packs for your stack.
The strongest rules are in context from the first turn, sent again when the context compacts, and a mandatory violation is blocked.
Sensei. The stronger rule wins. Then the closer one.
